source.title: Adaptive and Explicit safe: Triggering Latent Safety Awareness in Large Reasoning Models
source.authors: Kehao Miao; Jia-Xin Li; Hong-Liang Chen; Yu-Ke Hu; Zhan Qin

page_placements.theme: Explicit and intermediate safety reasoning can improve robustness

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a structured safety analysis placed after reasoning and before the final answer can improve safety under harmful and jailbreak prompts. This is a different training method from the token-level KL measurement or fine-tuning interventions in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test fine-tuning on harmful examples or benign-only data, per-token KL divergence, compliant prefills, or safety localization in parameters. Its entropy analysis is not a measure of aligned-versus-base KL. The safety-rate rows test the paper's structured-trigger training method against harmful and jailbreak benchmarks. The entropy figures are recorded as related findings under none.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes Safe Trigger, a safety-alignment method for reasoning models that inserts a <safe> analysis block between reasoning and the final answer. Its results compare its own method's harmful and jailbreak ASR against Base, Star1 and SafePath. It never tests whether safety is concentrated in the first tokens. It does not check whether its method spreads safety beyond the opening or survives prefill, harmful fine-tuning or decoding attacks, which is the V7 question. The 'Alignment Depth' section borrows Qi et al.'s entropy analysis as an evaluation tool, applied only to responses already judged safe. So the ASR drops are mitigation performance, not a test of any version. They belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also claim a 'Latent Safety Awareness' finding (Table 2): LRMs re-shown their own reasoning identify risks at 44.79–100% rates. They also say the pipeline is self-bootstrapped, without manual annotation or closed-source models.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains LRMs to insert structured safety analysis after reasoning and then applies DPO; it does not reproduce harmful-example fine-tuning, benign-data fine-tuning, or aligned/base per-token KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and benchmark. Qwen3-32B has an already-zero Base rate on XsTest Unsafe; Safe Trigger entropy findings are reported only for conditionally sampled safe responses on 100 AdvBench queries.

fits_no_version.finding: Safe Trigger SFT/DPO lowers LlamaGuard-judged ASR on harmful and jailbreak benchmarks across four LRMs. Example: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B WildJailbreak drops from 32.45% to 1.45% with ST-D. Some cells change little: Qwen3-32B PAP 12% to 10% with ST-S, and XsTest-unsafe sits at the 0% floor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training reasoning models to insert a self-generated safety analysis after reasoning reduces harmful and jailbreak compliance while preserving general capability.

fits_no_version.finding: Among AdvBench prompts that every method answered safely, Safe Trigger models show lower first-token and cumulative early entropy than Base. Star1 and SafePath are in between.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-trained reasoning models differ in early-decoding confidence on safe responses.

record.problems: The token-entropy results are shown in figures without exact values in the text. Safety rates use LlamaGuard-3-8B as an automatic discriminator; the paper does not report uncertainty estimates for the tabulated rates. The entropy analysis is restricted to prompts on which all five methods produced judged-safe responses.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, Table 4 aggregate averages and Figure 4 trigger-activation rates were not separately included; Table 3 provides the per-model, per-benchmark safety-rate results. Figure 5 inference-length results do not measure a claim version.

untested.parts: No benign-only fine-tuning condition measuring harmful compliance.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attack. Jailbreaks (WildJailbreak, MSJ, PAP) are prompt-level, not attacks that get past the opening tokens.
LoRA is used for training only; no localization test.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.
The method is not tested for spreading safety beyond the first tokens. It is not tested for robustness to prefill or fine-tuning attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 'supports' label and the Qwen3-32B XsTest 'limits_scope' label should both be dropped. The XsTest case is a 0% floor, not a qualification of the claim. Neither original source is this study. Safety judgments come from LlamaGuard-3-8B and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples with unsafe target responses.
No benign-only fine-tuning condition; general examples are part of a safety-training mixture.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL on harmful prompts. The paper measures entropy for safe responses, not the claimed KL distribution.
No compliant prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test of bypassing safety.
LoRA is used, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether the data or training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Tests safety outcomes for structured analysis after reasoning, but does not measure whether safety is distributed across response positions or whether it survives compliant prefill.

rows.subject: Qwen3-8B
rows.check: These rows compare the study's own method (ST-S/ST-D) with the untrained base model on ASR. The method is not a deepening intervention in V7's sense: it spreads no safety signal across response positions and is not tested against prefill or fine-tuning attacks. They should not be linked to V7. The reader's per-row states (observed/partial/absent) only describe method effectiveness. r27 and r33 (Qwen3-32B XsTest, base 0.00%) are floor effects, not evidence about any version.
